<h2 id="qa-da985f94e4904b1e">How does SLiC-HF&#x27;s hinge margin differ from DPO&#x27;s reference-relative one?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aslic-hf">SLiC-HF</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The hinge directly constrains sequence likelihood differences alongside supervision. DPO contrasts log ratios relative to a frozen policy. Both baseline and loss shape differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Once the hinge margin is met, ranking penalty can stop; reference-relative preference is different.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10425">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2305.10425-slic-hf/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-da985f94e4904b1e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:slic-hf" data-paper-title="SLiC-HF" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1991e69bbbffe205">Why can SLiC-HF use pairs collected by another model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aslic-hf">SLiC-HF</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google DeepMind</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The objective can score fixed responses and doesn&#x27;t need current-policy samples. Keep sources and same-prompt pairing. Local candidate calculations are not the paper&#x27;s T5 and human evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Old summaries can be scored by the current policy if labels still belong to those summaries.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rrhf" data-paper-title="RRHF" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<span id="paper-post-training-rrhf-c28f5ad3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-25f8a4e90ddf8a40">Why use a full ordering of multiple same-prompt answers in RRHF?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arrhf">RRHF</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba DAMO Academy</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Multi-source responses provide more relative comparisons than one pair. Match length-averaged log likelihood to reward order and supervise the best answer. Ranking quality depends on labels/reward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Good, middling and poor responses supply several orderings, not one winner pair.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.05302">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2304.05302-rrhf/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-25f8a4e90ddf8a40">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rrhf" data-paper-title="RRHF" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c84c0f92798e6391">Why still apply SFT to the best answer after ranking responses?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arrhf">RRHF</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba DAMO Academy</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The hinge only fixes ordering conflicts and can stop giving a useful generation signal once sorted. SFT raises high-quality content likelihood. External rewards and length normalization do not guarantee factual correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Even with three answers ranked correctly, the best may be rare; its SFT term can still increase likelihood.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.05302">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2304.05302-rrhf/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c84c0f92798e6391">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:rrhf" data-paper-title="RRHF" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">

<h2 id="qa-5870e025a2c47fef">What do best-response SFT and RRHF ranking each add?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arrhf">RRHF</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba DAMO Academy</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ranking corrects relative order; SFT directly raises best-response likelihood. Ranking alone can succeed by suppressing alternatives. The combination isn&#x27;t a universal optimum.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A good answer should be learned, not merely score above a bad one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.05302">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2304.05302-rrhf/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5870e025a2c47fef">Question link</a></p>
</details>

<h2 id="qa-5bdec3da01bf0a15">Why isn&#x27;t RRHF p_i raw probability?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Arrhf">RRHF</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Alibaba DAMO Academy</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It is length-normalized response log probability. The hinge compares this order within one prompt with consistent reward direction. Candidate tests do not reproduce full 7B training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Using decimal probabilities in place of mean logp changes margins and gradients.</p>

<h2 id="qa-3a349cd4a2fb2d2f">What role does the constitution play in Constitutional AI?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aconstitutional-ai">Constitutional AI</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Anthropic</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Explicit natural-language principles guide critique, revision and AI preference judgments. They supply human supervision, not absolute values discovered by the model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use a stated principle to explain a revision instead of an unexplained good/bad score.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

</details>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:constitutional-ai" data-paper-title="Constitutional AI" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">

<h2 id="qa-c8b07171181a7608">Why are critique/revision and AI preference training separate stages?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aconstitutional-ai">Constitutional AI</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Anthropic</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>First critique and revise by principles, then supervise the revised texts. Next compare responses by those principles and use preference learning for RL. Demonstrations and choice labels differ. Principles and local updates do not establish harmlessness or full red teaming.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rewrite a reply to avoid privacy leakage, then compare two rewrites; text and winner labels are distinct inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.08073">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2212.08073-constitutional-ai/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c8b07171181a7608">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:constitutional-ai" data-paper-title="Constitutional AI" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">LLM post-training / Preference and alignment: identify the feedback first</a></p>

<h2 id="qa-0d13ae16bfabf670">Why distinguish principle-based revision SFT from RLAIF?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aconstitutional-ai">Constitutional AI</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Anthropic</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The former learns revised text; the latter uses AI preferences to train reward and optimize policy. Data and execution differ. Local simplification does not establish a separate preference model or PPO; arithmetic principles are not safety red-team evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Repairing one answer supplies a demonstration, not evidence of completed reward-driven RL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.08073">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../post-training/2212.08073-constitutional-ai/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0d13ae16bfabf670">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="post-training:constitutional-ai" data-paper-title="Constitutional AI" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="post-training" data-theme="post-training" data-topic="post-training/preference-and-alignment">

<h2 id="qa-2199338594cbccc3">What safety claims do local Constitutional AI principles support?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=post-training%3Aconstitutional-ai">Constitutional AI</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Anthropic</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Deterministic axes such as correctness, format, process and brevity test principle scoring and state updates. They do not cover real harmful requests or train a complete safety reward model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Valid formatting doesn&#x27;t establish reliable refusal of dangerous advice.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<details class="ar-learning-guide" markdown="1"><summary>Topic guide and reading order</summary>

## Start with this question

How do we turn pairwise preferences or a thumbs-up on one answer into a trainable objective?

## Takeaway

DPO uses preferred and rejected answers to the same prompt and classifies preferences through the current-to-reference policy log ratio. KTO uses individually desirable or undesirable feedback without pairs. Reward models, AI raters, and controllable SFT change the source or organization of feedback. The feedback format, reference distribution, and annotation reliability constrain the objective; algorithm names alone do not justify swapping losses.

## Example

A support system may have ranked pairs for one group and accept/reject labels on individual answers for another. Use true same-prompt pairs for DPO, not arbitrary pairs from different questions. If groups disagree on style, retain preference distributions and annotation provenance so a judge's style preference is not mistaken for factual correctness.

## Common pitfall

Better preference scores do not guarantee facts, safety, or production gains. Match data, reference model, and evaluation, and check length/style confounds. Closed-form losses, candidate policies, and preference fixtures validate their own mechanisms. A scorer contract or an unreproduced experiment does not show the model is aligned.

## Reading order

Read DPO for paired feedback and the reference log ratio, then KTO for unpaired binary feedback, then probabilistic Autorater for confidence distributions rather than a single winner.

1. [DPO](../../../../post-training/2305.18290-dpo/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.18290)
2. [KTO](../../../../post-training/2402.01306-kto/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.01306)
3. [Judging with Confidence: Calibrating Autoraters to Preference Distributions](../../../../post-training/2510.00263-probabilistic-autorater/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.00263v1)

## Check your understanding

Can a liked answer and a disliked answer to a different question form a DPO pair?

??? note "Show suggested answer"

    Usually not. Standard DPO compares answers under the same condition. Cross-question pairing confounds difficulty and content. Collect same-prompt alternatives or use an unpaired objective with explicit label distribution, reference policy, and independent evaluation.

</details>
